### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **37** documentable anchor(s).

**40** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 197fbe2c04edbe4cf0ffc691dc59e4fcf8d9ba47`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **37** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 197fbe2c04edbe4cf0ffc691dc59e4fcf8d9ba47` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `051c475fe75494b350771faebdd7611ac9586d72` — the merge of head `faae1c0de170a2c87a97e334e018f8a048834d0e` into base `197fbe2c04edbe4cf0ffc691dc59e4fcf8d9ba47`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 051c475fe75494b350771faebdd7611ac9586d72 && git checkout 051c475fe75494b350771faebdd7611ac9586d72
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 197fbe2c04edbe4cf0ffc691dc59e4fcf8d9ba47 faae1c0de170a2c87a97e334e018f8a048834d0e && git checkout -B drift-repro 197fbe2c04edbe4cf0ffc691dc59e4fcf8d9ba47 && git merge --no-ff faae1c0de170a2c87a97e334e018f8a048834d0e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 197fbe2c04edbe4cf0ffc691dc59e4fcf8d9ba47
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 197fbe2c04edbe4cf0ffc691dc59e4fcf8d9ba47` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `faae1c0de170a2c87a97e334e018f8a048834d0e`
Local-runs: none

Rendered 2026-10-13T11:22Z by the adopting seat's session, read-only, against AGENTS.md Prime Directives #10 and #12, Route and surface ownership, Post-Task Checklist step 3, and ADR-0069. Read: the net diff against `main` (merge base `01a3421f42`; 10 files, +1325 / -28, equal to the three-dot diff), the six branch commits and the two merges of `main`, the card thread (body, triage `6140946784`, claim `6141924281`, report `6144103571`, and the ACCEPT `6144168932` read as a claim to test), ruling `6141053341` with PR #23200's landed changeset and doors on `origin/main`, the slice-1 records on PR #23133 (`6138381862`, `6139157658`), PR #23242's body and file list, the head's check-runs, and at this head the sources the diff leans on: core's `auth-gate.ts`, `authz-store-unavailable.ts` and `resolve-authz-context.ts`; runtime's `api-endpoint-step.ts`, `http-dispatcher.ts` and `error-envelope.ts`; rest's `rest-server.ts`, `rest-api-plugin.ts` and `direct-mount-composition.ts`; cloud-connection's `marketplace-proxy-plugin.ts`; the three package entries and `exports` maps. Nothing was built, run or re-run; the built-declaration claims are judged from the entries and the module shapes, not from a rebuild. This record stays at function level (triage `6140946784`): sites, functions and the class of session refused. The route-level boot readings are the seat's, relied on and never quoted.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, judged at this head.

1. **One decision, no copy — right.** Five sites, one predicate. The fallback (`applyEndpointPolicies`, step ②), `CloudConnectionPlugin`'s `sessionFromAuthService` and `MarketplaceInstallLocalPlugin.resolveInstallPrincipal` call core's `evaluateAuthGate`; `refusePackageRequest` and `refuseFederationRequest` read the `authGate` that `RestServer.computeExecCtx` lifts through core's `normalizeAuthGate`, the field `enforceAuth` reads. No site spells the allow-list, touches a route list or re-derives the decision; the pins import `isAuthGateAllowlisted` only to assert census facts. No new export or exported field: all three `exports` maps publish `.` alone; `packages/runtime/src/index.ts` takes `createDispatcherPlugin` and `DispatcherPluginConfig` from `dispatcher-plugin.js` and nothing from `endpoint-policy.js`, so `EndpointPolicyContext.resolveGatedSessionUser` is package-internal; `packages/rest/src/index.ts` re-exports neither registrar module nor `direct-mount-composition.js` (only `createRestApiPlugin` and its config type), so the `authGate` field on each registrar's option literal never reaches the entry; `packages/cloud-connection/src/index.ts` already exported both classes, and the new names are closures inside `start()` (`sessionFromAuthService`, `resolveSession`, the plugin's `refuseHeldSession`), a module-private function (install-local's `refuseHeldSession`), unexported interfaces (`ResolvedSession`, `InstallPrincipal`) and a private member (`resolveInstallPrincipal`) whose emitted stub carries no type. That is consistent with the measured declarations: runtime and rest byte-identical, cloud-connection differing by one prose hunk. One correction of label only: the hunk the report calls "the class docblock" is the module's file-header comment (`cloud-connection-plugin.ts` lines 23 to 28, plus the one-line note at 55); it is prose either way, and no declaration moves.
2. **`evaluateAuthGate(user, '')` — right, and fail-closed by construction.** `isAuthGateAllowlisted` opens with `if (!rawPath) return false;` (#7898), before the anchored route match and before the parameterised rows, so an empty path can never earn an exemption and no declared path, under any host prefix, can exempt itself; the anti-bypass pin drives the host-prefix shape after asserting its precondition. Gating `authRequired: false` endpoints is right under ADR-0069 D3 ("gated out of all protected resources") and under both model seams: the fallback runs the target as the caller's execution context (`resolveRequestScope`), so a held session would read and write as its user; REST skips `enforceAuth` only for `anonymousPublicRead`, which is `!context?.userId` AND a public-audience read (`rest-server.ts` line 5505), so a signed-in caller is gated on a public read too; the dispatcher asks `enforceAuthGate` inside `dispatch()` before any domain resolves. The new session read is safe: `readGatedSessionUser` reads nothing unless `isAuthGateActive()` answers `true` (a false or throwing probe yields `undefined` with no read); reads once with `inProcessSessionReadInput` (no cookie renewal, #22258); and on a failed read throws `AuthzStoreUnavailableError('auth_gate', err)`, whose own `status` is 503 and `code` is `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`. `runAppEndpointStep` has no catch around `applyEndpointPolicies`, so the throw reaches the fallback's `errorResponse`, which reads `err.status`; the outage pin reads 503 with nothing run. The read hands `session?.user` to the predicate and nowhere else; the execution context the target runs as is built by `resolveRequestScope`, untouched, so nothing is minted or widened. Placement between the meter and `authRequired` mirrors `enforceAuth`'s gate-before-floor order, and the separate read is necessary: `resolveSessionPrincipalId` swallows every failure as anonymous, and `http-dispatcher.ts` never lifts `authGate` onto the context it resolves, so there was nothing to reuse.
3. **REST's direct mounts — right.** Both registrars receive the one resolver `rest-api-plugin.ts` binds (`restServer.resolvePackageRouteExecutionContext`, which is `resolveExecCtx` over `computeExecCtx`), so the `authGate` they read is the one `enforceAuth` reads. `refusePackageRequest` is the publish handler's first statement and refuses on `ctx?.authGate` before `shouldDenyAnonymous` and before the capability check; `refuseFederationRequest` refuses before its anonymous floor and its capability check, on every handler that opens with it (five). Each writes `sendError(res, 403, code, message)`, the module's declared nested envelope (`check:route-envelope` pins `package-routes` at zero unenveloped), which is the door's own, as the card and claim require; REST's `enforceAuth` keeps its flat body on its own seam. Neither module registers an OPTIONS handler, so a preflight never enters the refusal and no counterpart to `enforceAuth`'s OPTIONS skip is owed.
4. **cloud-connection — right.** `CloudConnectionPlugin`: every session on the surface comes from `resolveSession`, whose two arms (the host kernel's `auth` in single-environment mode, the environment kernel's `auth` in multi-tenant mode) both end in `sessionFromAuthService`, where the one consult sits; the module admits no inbound API key (the bearers it builds are outbound, to the control plane), and each of the seven session doors refuses on `session?.authGate` before its 401 and before any control-plane call. `MarketplaceInstallLocalPlugin`: all five routes reach `refuseHeldSession` through one of two call sites, the listing door's own `resolveInstallPrincipal` call and `requireInstallCapability` for the four mutating doors; the module's other session reads (`resolveActiveOrgId`) sit in post-admission helpers (`sampleDataInScope`, `handlePurge` after its admission, `applySideEffects`). An API-key caller is unaffected, as on REST: core's `resolveAuthzContext` resolves the key first and calls the `getSession` bridge only when no key resolved a user, so `sessionUser` stays unset and the predicate answers null. Because both plugins read identity and posture in one read, a failed read has no identity either and stays the 401 it already was; that is PR #23200's datasource-admin shape (one read, 401), while the fallback and the publish door are its storage shape (a second read, 503).
5. **Ruling A on the two no-session doors — right.** `CloudConnectionPlugin`'s status read makes no session read (the census pin asserts zero reads on it), and `marketplace-proxy-plugin.ts` contains no session or auth-service read at all. ADR-0069 D3 holds a session out of PROTECTED resources; a door that answers a cookieless caller identically protects nothing by session, and a held session there gets exactly the anonymous answer, so no held-session path is left open on either. The card places the consult "where they resolve their session", and they resolve none. `Fixes #23190` stays right; the PR body and the changeset both say which two doors are unchanged and why, so nothing is buried.
6. **Parity with PR #23200 — right.** Same predicate call (`evaluateAuthGate(user, '')`), same answer (403 with the gate's `code` and `message` in the family's declared envelope), same order (the gate, then the anonymous floor, then the capability), the same 503 posture where a second read exists and the same single-read 401 where it does not. The two halves have not diverged.

### ② Semver level

**Right.** `.changeset/23190-auth-gate-cli-sites.md` (24 lines): `minor` for `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/rest` and `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, all three publishing (`private` absent, `18.0.0-next.0`); the body's first line is `fix(runtime,rest,cloud-connection)!: …`; `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` exactly once, with #23200's continuation; exactly one `adr-0087:` marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, in the HTML-comment form; the launch-window BREAKING line exactly once; and a "What changes for you" paragraph, which is the migration text step 3 asks a breaking changeset to carry. That is PR #23200's changeset line for line in shape and category, and the shape the #23133 records (`6138381862` remedy, `6139157658` PASS) settled for an accept-set narrowing. The marker's facts hold on the diff: no path under `packages/spec`, no removed exported declaration (the removed lines are a comment rewrite, an inline return type moved into the unexported `InstallPrincipal`, and a closure's return type), and the new fields live on package-internal types only (① item 1). The PR title carries the bang; body line 1 is `Fixes #23190`, line 2 the Clause-② line with its continuation. `Check Changeset` on this head is `success`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`dispatcher-plugin.ts` touched** — under the claim's condition: the fallback's session read is wired there (`readGatedSessionUser` and the `resolveGatedSessionUser` binding). `api-endpoint-step.ts` and `marketplace-proxy-plugin.ts` are untouched; no ledger rows, and `check:engine-double-contract` is green. Right.
- **Deepened history** — an object-store fetch on the shared checkout, no file edit; the lost race on `refs/remotes/origin/main` is a sibling's fetch, not this PR's. Carried; nothing owed.
- **Two temporary measurement files** — deleted before commit; the PR's ten files carry neither. Checklist step 7 honoured.
- **Two merges of `main`** (`8fe7a39bb2`, `faae1c0de1`) — each is byte-identical to its branch parent over the ten paths (both diffs empty); what `main` brought under the three packages (`domains/meta.ts` and others) is disjoint. Right.
- **Commit trailers** — the model-free pair, as the #23133 record already ruled. No action.
- **Disclosure** — the PR body, changeset, report and ACCEPT stay at function level; the pin files name the routes they drive, which is source, not a reach reading.
- **`open_questions[0]`** — ruled A by the seat; judged right in ① item 5.
- **Carried note 1, the dispatcher's own seam fails open** — verified: `HttpDispatcher.enforceAuthGate` swallows the session read's rejection and its outer `catch` returns `null` ("fail-open — never break dispatch on a gate hiccup"), so an active gate whose read throws admits the request on every dispatcher route, while REST answers 503 in the same window by the #13906 ruling (decision 2 option B), on the reasoning that a declared enforcement must not vanish silently. Not a defect this PR must fix: the dispatcher's seam is outside the claim's surface, and the card's acceptance does not name it. ⛔ Not rightly carried either. It is a measured divergence between the two model seams on exactly the window the maintainer ruled for REST; core's `auth-gate.ts` header says the seams "can never drift on what is blocked"; and the dev drove it through `dispatch()` and read 200. Under Prime Directive #10 that is a contract reading with its evidence named, and an acceptance note is where it will not be acted on. **Escalated: the seat files it as a card** (`domain:cli`, `http-dispatcher.ts`, `enforceAuthGate`'s outage window), carrying the dev's measurement and the #13906 ruling text, for triage to decide whether that ruling extends to the dispatcher.
- **Carried note 2, the federation floor answers an outage 401** — verified: `computeExecCtx`'s outer catch rethrows the branded outage (`rest-server.ts` line 3357, `rethrowAuthzStoreUnavailable`), `refusePackageRequest` relays it as 503 through the same helper, and `refuseFederationRequest`'s bare `catch`, which sets `authz` to `undefined`, turns the same throw into `401 UNAUTHENTICATED`. Core's `rethrowAuthzStoreUnavailable` header names that exact net (the catch every fail-closed seam between the resolver and a door should use in place of one that returns undefined) and that exact disguise. Two registrars mounted by one composition step, on one resolver, answer one outage two ways. It predates this PR (the floor landed in August, before #13906), and this PR's gate adds nothing to the window. Not this PR's to fix: outside the card's acceptance, and Prime Directive #10 forbids the scope creep. ⛔ Not rightly carried: the contract text and the code are both named, which is what the filing gate asks for. **Escalated: the seat files it as a card** (`domain:cli`, `external-datasource-routes.ts`, `refuseFederationRequest`'s catch), a one-site conversion onto `rethrowAuthzStoreUnavailable` with the REST pin's publish outage case as its template.
- **Check-runs on this head** at render time: 30 `success`, 8 `skipped` (Console Pin Gate, the live-database gates, the opt-in tarball smoke and the label and size jobs, as this diff's paths warrant), 0 failure; `Test Core (3/6)` was still `in_progress` and is not judged here. `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, every Lint and Type Check run, `Build Core`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Part-of PR must not also close its card` and `The card this PR closes must claim this branch` are `success`. The landing waits for that shard as for every other check; nothing in it can move a judgment above, since the three suites and the pins also ran at this head in the report.
- **Not governed** — none of the ten paths is a governed surface; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` agrees.

Everything in ① and ② holds. ③ carries two escalations to the seat, neither a finding against this head.
